doc.title: Don Alias interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002

title: Selling out and critics
summary: They discuss critics accusing popular musicians of selling out, such as George Benson, and trite formulaic music.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: It’s curious, sometimes it’s like well if you want to be really respected don’t make too much money. Because then the critics will say you sold out somehow.

Sure. How many times have they done that? They did it to George Benson when he started to sing. And I say more power to it, because those guys do it good. It’s the guys that don’t do it good on 101.9 where it really does sound trite. You know they’re selling out, when you hear all those trite melodies.
Yeah, it’s like there’s that formula. You know the thing that I judge, as soon as that song is over, do you have any remembrance of that song?
